item.title: Equivariant Steklov homogenisation and stability of spectral representations
item.description: arXiv:2610.12725v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that isolated spectral clusters preserve their finite-group representation under equivariant spectral convergence. In particular, an irreducible limiting eigenspace cannot split into several nearby eigenvalues, while an isotypic limiting eigenspace imposes corresponding divisibility constraints on the multiplicities in the approximating cluster. We then construct a one-parameter equivariant Steklov homogenisation on closed orientable surfaces, allowing Laplace spectral representations to be transferred to Steklov spectral clusters. Applied to the hyperbolic surfaces of Fortier Bourque, Gruda-Mediavilla, Petri, and Pineault, this yields first Steklov multiplicities 16 and 21 in genera 10 and 17, and at least 24 in genus 37. These examples give counterexamples to Jammes's conjecture on first Steklov multiplicity.
item.dc:creator: Samuel Audet-Beaumont, Maxime Fortier Bourque, Alexandre Girouard

item.title: High-Index Asymptotics of Mathieu Spectral Gaps and Splittings
item.description: arXiv:2610.12751v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Consider the Mathieu operator $L=-d^2/dx^2+2a\cos(2x)$ for fixed $a\in\mathbb{C}\setminus\{0\}$. For large enough $n$, the periodic ($n$ even) or anti-periodic ($n$ odd) problem on $[0,\pi]$ has exactly two algebraically simple eigenvalues $\lambda_n^-,\lambda_n^+$ in the disc $|\lambda-n^2|<1$. We prove that, as $n\to\infty$, $\lambda_n^+-\lambda_n^-=\pm\frac{8(a/4)^n}{[(n-1)!]^2}\exp\left[-\frac{a^2(n+2)}{4(n^2-1)^2}-\frac{15a^4}{128n^7}+O(n^{-8})\right]$, where the sign depends on the labelling. For real $a$ with $\lambda_n^-<\lambda_n^+$, this difference is the length of the $n$th spectral gap. Expanding the exponential determines the relative corrections of orders $n^{-4}$ to $n^{-7}$, beyond the correction $-a^2/(4n^3)$ obtained by Anahtarci and Djakov (2012) with a relative $O(n^{-4})$ remainder. By isospectrality, the same formula holds for the potential $ce^{-2ix}+de^{2ix}$ with $a^2=cd\ne0$.
item.dc:creator: Berkay Anahtarci

item.title: Quantitative spectral stability and sharp Fourier estimates for periodic CMV matrices with decaying perturbations
item.description: arXiv:2610.12856v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study half-line CMV matrices whose Verblunsky coefficients are decaying perturbations of periodic sequences. We quantify the stability of fine properties of the absolutely continuous spectral measure under such perturbations. More precisely, we establish H\"older continuity of the perturbed spectral measure and derive sharp time-averaged Fourier estimates governing the associated quantum dynamics. These results remain valid up to the edges of the absolutely continuous spectrum. Since the spectral measure of a half-line CMV matrix is precisely the orthogonality measure for the corresponding orthogonal polynomials on the unit circle (OPUC), our results also yield new statements for OPUC whose Verblunsky coefficients are decaying perturbations of periodic sequences.
item.dc:creator: Moacir Aloisio, C\'esar R. de Oliveira, Mariane Pigossi

item.title: On the inequality $\mu_3 < \lambda_1$ for the eigenvalues of the Laplace operator
item.description: arXiv:2610.13180v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 1952, P\'olya proved the inequality $\mu_2 < \lambda_1$ for the eigenvalues of Dirichlet and Neumann problems in domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^d$, $d \ge 2$. We show that $\mu_3 < \lambda_1$ if $d\ge 3$. In the two-dimensional case, in 2025, Rohleder proved that $\mu_3 < \lambda_1$ for simply connected domains. We prove that this inequality holds also true for double connected domains symmetric with respect to the origin.
item.dc:creator: N. Filonov

item.title: Sums of Dirichlet eigenvalues in proximity of the disk and the ball
item.description: arXiv:2610.13256v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive second order perturbation expansions of volume-normalized sums of the first $n$ Dirichlet eigenvalues for near-circular and near-spherical domains. The disk (resp. ball) is only a critical shape when $n$ is the last index of an eigenvalue cluster, and in dimension two and three our expansions yield a finitely checkable criterion deciding whether the disk or ball is a weak local minimizer or a saddle point. In two dimensions, this allows us to show that there is an infinite number of cases in which the disk is a saddle point for finite eigenvalue sums.
item.dc:creator: Matthias Baur

item.title: Non-resonant angles in a Robin eigenvalue problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.13601v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In an earlier study of the Laplacian eigenvalues with strongly attractive Robin boundary conditions in polygons it was found that if each corner is either concave or non-resonant, then the asymptotic behavior of the individual eigenvalues is determined by an effective one-dimensional operator on the boundary with Dirichlet boundary conditions at the corners. The non-resonance condition was formulated in terms of an eigenvalue bound on truncated sectors, and it was only shown to be satisfied by the right and obtuse opening angles. In the present work, we determine the full range of non-resonant angles: it turns out that the non-resonance condition fails only for the opening angles $\frac{\pi}{2n+1}$ with $n=1,2,3,\dots$, and these critical values are equivalently characterized in terms of the jumps of the eigenvalue counting function and the existence of bounded generalized eigenfunctions. This resolves the numerically supported conjecture stated by Dauge and Lafranche.
item.dc:creator: Konstantin Pankrashkin

item.title: Non-Bloch band theory for finite banded non-Hermitian Toeplitz matrices
item.description: arXiv:2610.13715v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Non-Bloch band theory recovers the open-boundary spectrum of a non-Hermitian chain from its Bloch Hamiltonian evaluated along the generalised Brillouin zone rather than the unit circle. We develop its finite-size counterpart for banded Toeplitz matrices with real open-boundary spectrum. Reality of the spectrum forces the generalised Brillouin zone to be parametrised by an analytic polar curve, so the known sufficient condition for a real spectrum is also necessary under some mild non-degeneracy conditions. At finite size $n$, the eigenvalues of the original and the symmetrised Bloch Hamiltonians are given by samples at $n$ quantised momenta from the same limiting band, although separated by a phase mismatch of order $1/n$ which we obtain in closed form. Iterating this correction $K$ times yields a quantisation rule on the generalised Brillouin zone reproducing the finite spectrum with an error $\mathcal{O}(n^{-K-1})$ for any fixed $K$. At finite size, the generalised Brillouin zone itself is unchanged and only its parametrisation depends on $n$.
item.dc:creator: Yannick de Bruijn, Erik Orvehed Hiltunen

item.title: Sharp upper bounds for Steklov eigenvalues on warped products
item.description: arXiv:2610.13738v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We obtain sharp isoperimetric-type upper bounds for Steklov eigenvalues on warped products whose bases are compact Riemannian manifolds with boundary and whose fibres are closed Riemannian manifolds. These bounds involve the volume of the warped product and of its boundary, as well as the eigenvalues of the Laplace operator on the fibre and the Steklov eigenvalues of the base. After separation of variables, these bounds are obtained by comparison with auxiliary Helmholtz-Steklov problems on the base involving weighted Laplace operators naturally induced by the warping function. We also study the effect of various natural geometric constraints, such as the warping function being identically equal to one on the boundary. The proofs make use of various spectral approximation methods, including homogenisation on manifolds when the fibres are one-dimensional.
item.dc:creator: Jade Brisson, Bruno Colbois, Alexandre Girouard, Katie Gittins, Jean Lagac\'e-Taylor

item.title: Strict Dirichlet P\'olya Inequality for Simply Connected Planar Domains
item.description: arXiv:2610.13139v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish the strict Dirichlet P\'olya inequality on every bounded simply connected planar domain. The proof uses a unitary boundary transport formulation of the Helmholtz equation and relates Dirichlet resonances to unitary eigenphase crossings through the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map. An exact area identity yields the sharp Weyl coefficient, while a Ky Fan estimate leaves a strictly positive remainder in the counting estimate. The general case follows by conformal exhaustion.
item.dc:creator: Quanyu Tang, Zuoqin Wang

item.title: Harmonic analysis and circuit approximation of Sobolev functions on quantum input spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.13477v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We derive approximation rates for Sobolev functions defined on the complex unit sphere and complex projective space, representing quantum states, and on the special and projective unitary groups, representing quantum unitary operations. By using harmonic analysis on compact groups and compact homogeneous spaces, we characterize the corresponding Peter--Weyl decompositions and Sobolev spaces via irreducible representations and the Laplace--Beltrami operator. Combining spectral truncation with finite-depth quantum-circuit approximation, invoking the Solovay--Kitaev theorem, we establish quantitative rates that separate the spectral truncation error from the circuit approximation error.
item.dc:creator: Philipp Schmocker

item.title: Spectral Theory and Descriptive Combinatorics for Non-Regular Borel pmp Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.13551v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We continue the systematic study initiated in arXiv:2602.05185 of the relationship between the spectral theory and descriptive combinatorics of bounded-degree Borel pmp graphs, particularly in the non-regular setting. We first adapt a classical result of Nikiforov to give a new spectral lower bound on the approximate measurable chromatic number. For certain non-regular graphs, this bound improves on the approximate measurable version of Hoffman's classical bound established in arXiv:2602.05185. Next, we strengthen a characterization in arXiv:2602.05185 of approximate measurable bipartiteness in terms of the spectrum of the adjacency operator by generalizing to the case of non-regular graphs. Finally, we introduce the measurable domination number and adapt several classical results of Lu, Liu, and Tian to give a bound on the spectral gap of the Laplacian operator in terms of the measurable domination number.
item.dc:creator: Cecelia Higgins, Pieter Spaas, Sofia Torelli

item.title: An inverse spectral problem for the wave equation with a varying Robin parameter at the boundary
item.description: arXiv:2610.13629v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: An inverse spectral problem for a $(1+1)$-dimensional wave equation with wave speed $c(x)$ is considered. The spectral data consist of the eigenvalues of the Neumann--Dirichlet problem for the operator $-c^2(x)\partial_x^2$ together with their derivatives with respect to a Robin parameter at the boundary. We propose a two-step recovery procedure. In the first step, the Neumann-to-Dirichlet map $\Lambda$ is reconstructed from the spectral data using the results of arXiv/0406582. In the second step, the reconstructed $\Lambda$ is used within the regularization strategy for the boundary control method presented in arXiv:1509.04478. As an improvement, the regularization of the control problems employs a weighted combination of $L^2$ and $H^1$ penalty terms, and we prove a uniform convergence result for the family of optimal controls, thereby allowing the regularization parameters to be tuned simultaneously. We also prove that the forward spectral map, which assigns to a wave speed its spectral data, is Lipschitz continuous, and that the inverse spectral map underlying the reconstruction procedure is H\"older continuous on a subclass of wave speeds. The method is implemented numerically and validated on both smooth and piecewise smooth wave speed profiles. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the recovery of the wave speed exhibits high accuracy and robustness.
item.dc:creator: Antti Hannukainen, Petr Kulikov, Matti Lassas, Lauri Oksanen

item.title: Improved fractal Weyl bounds for convex cocompact hyperbolic surfaces and large resonance-free regions
item.description: arXiv:2301.03023v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $X$ be a convex cocompact hyperbolic surface, and let $\delta$ denote the Hausdorff dimension of its limit set. Let $N_X(\sigma,T)$ denote the number of resonances of $X$ inside the box $[\sigma, \delta] + i[0,T]$. We prove that for all $\sigma > \delta/2$, we have \[ N_X(\sigma,T) \ll_\epsilon T^{1 + \delta - 2(2\sigma - \delta) + \epsilon}. \] This strengthens the previously established "improved" fractal Weyl bounds due to Naud \cite{Naud14} and Dyatlov \cite{Dya19}. Moreover, this result implies that for every $\epsilon > 0$, there exist resonance-free rectangular boxes of arbitrary height within the strip \[ \left\{\, s \in \mathbb{C} : \tfrac{3}{4}\delta + \epsilon < \mathrm{Re}(s) < \delta\, \right\}. \] Our proof combines Naud's approach \cite{Naud14} with the refined transfer operator machinery developed by Dyatlov-Zworski \cite{DyZw18}, as well as a new estimate for oscillatory integrals that arise naturally in our analysis.
item.dc:creator: Louis Soares

item.title: Elementary commutator method for the Dirac equation with long-range perturbations
item.description: arXiv:2511.08209v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present direct and elementary commutator techniques for the Dirac equation with long-range electric and mass perturbations. The main results are absence of generalized eigenfunctions and locally uniform resolvent estimates, both in terms of the optimal Besov-type spaces. With an additional massless assumption, we also obtain an algebraic radiation condition of projection type. For their proofs, following the scheme of Ito-Skibsted, we adopt, along with various weight functions, the generator of radial translations as conjugate operator, and avoid any of advanced functional analysis, pseudodifferential calculus, or even reduction to the Schr\"odinger equation. The results of the paper would serve as a foundation for the stationary scattering theory of the Dirac operator.
item.dc:creator: Shinichi Arita, Kenichi Ito

item.title: A Lower Bound for the First Non-zero Basic Eigenvalue on a Singular Riemannian Foliation
item.description: arXiv:2602.17501v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In the paper, we provide a lower bound of the first non-zero basic eigenvalue on a closed singular Riemannian manifold $(M^n,\mathcal{F})$ having basic mean curvature that depends on the given lower bound of the Ricci curvature $Ric(M)\geq (n-1)K$ and the diameter of the leaf space $d_{M/\mathcal{F}}$. For foliations given by points, the results cover estimates of the first non-zero eigenvalues lower bounds, which are Zhong-Yang estimate, Yang estimate and Shi-Yang estimate. We also show a rigidity result that corresponds to the case of $Ric(M)\geq 0$. This is a generalization of Hang-Wang rigidity, which is the equality case of Zhong-Yang estimate.
item.dc:creator: Bach Tran
